name: Sene
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 2018. Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). Inaugural-Dissertation, Universität zu Köln. viii+331 pp. (KUPS 9757)
sources.note: Nothing for Sene. Comparative morphology only (author says the comparative phonology part is unwritten, Preface p. iii). Sene data come from Pilhofer 1928:200-17, 218ff, 298ff and McElhanon's fieldnotes (App. A/B/C). Only incidental diachronic remarks on accent: p. 97 Huon Tip emphatic pronoun 'presumably.. bore a heavy stress on the first syllable in discourse'; p. 160 Kâte-Mape present-tense forms 'presumably had a unitary word accent on the first syllable of the verb root' -- reconstructions, not a description of Sene stress.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG 'PNG Language Resources: Sene' (www-01.sil.org, 2007-2013, Internet Archive copy) and pnglanguages.sil.org language page sej (the Internet Archive 2024).
sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available' -- no SIL OPD, grammar or phonology exists for Sene.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1975. North-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 527-567. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Sec. 2.8.1.3.2.4 'Sene (EH-4), pop. less than ten. Kotte Census Division: Lakona' (p. 533); notes Lakona '(formerly SENE)' now speaks Wemo Kâte. General Finisterre-Huon phonology section has no stress statement; nothing on Sene stress.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU.
sources.harvard_location: Divinity School Library (offsite storage), call number - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354 .Z91
sources.note: Sene appears only in the language list; ch. 1 phonology (10 representative languages, Sene not among them) says nothing about stress/accent.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, 'Sene' language page (lexicon of c. 50 items from McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970).
sources.note: Word forms carry no stress marks; no prose on phonology.

sources.citation: Pilhofer, Georg. 1929 [1928-29]. Wörterverzeichnis aus zwölf Mundarten und Nachbarsprachen des Kâte. Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen 19: 41-69.
sources.note: Companion wordlist (c. 300 items) incl. Sene; its Vorbemerkung gives transcription conventions and may mark or comment on accent. Full view on Google Books (sVT-K_-mbmwC) and HathiTrust (uc1.b3347779), could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Pilhofer, Georg. 1928 [1927-28]. Formenlehre von zehn Mundarten und Nachbarsprachen des Kâte. Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen 18: 196-231, 298-315 (Lautlehre secs. 1-5, pp. 196-199; Sene verb morphology pp. 200-217, object verbs 218ff, cases 298ff).
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Sene (Pilhofer's own fieldwork before the shift to Kâte); its Lautlehre preamble is the one place a Betonung remark for Sene could exist. Public domain, full view: HathiTrust uc1.b3347778 / umn.319510018927392 (ZES v.17-18) and Google Books id 3CQsswFJepMC ('Volume 18') -- both could not be reached by automated download, readable from a US browser.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1967-2010s. Sene survey fieldnotes (word list and paradigms elicited at Lakona, 1967; rechecked for Suter's project). Unpublished, SIL-PNG / in Suter's possession.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern phonetic record of Sene; phonetic transcriptions may carry stress marks. Cited throughout Suter 2018 as 'McElhanon's fieldnotes'.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1967. Preliminary observations on Huon Peninsula languages. Oceanic Linguistics 6(1): 1-45.

sources.note: Survey report from McElhanon's 1967 Huon Peninsula fieldwork (which elicited Sene at Lakona); contains phonological observations across the Huon languages and may include a general or per-language stress remark covering Sene.

sources.citation: Pilhofer, Georg. 1933. Grammatik der Kâte-Sprache in Neuguinea. Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen, Beiheft 14. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.

sources.note: Full Lautlehre incl. Betonung/Ton for Kâte (Wemo) with notes on neighbouring dialects (Wamolâ etc.); the closest detailed phonological description in the Huon Tip group and the framework Pilhofer used for his 1928 dialect survey; would show whether his Sene transcriptions mark accent.
